review_notes: I read the whole target file. I compared its Hopf-ideal proof with the same-named proofs in UpperTriangularCoordinateRing.lean and UnitriangularCoordinateRing.lean, and with the determinant-one ideal in SpecialLinearCoordinateRing.lean. I also checked GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.lean for existing lemmas (native_antipode_matrix, native_comul_matrix, native_counit_matrix). I found no existing generic lemma that reduces generator-wise Hopf-ideal checks, or that gives the quotient antipode formula. I did not check whether Mathlib has one, beyond confirming `Ideal.IsHopfIdeal` is only the structure in Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Quotient.lean. The proposed lemma statements are sketches and have not been compiled. The type-class and `change` details (for example the local `CommRing` instance on the tensor product) may need adjusting. Two findings are reported: the generator-wise Hopf-ideal scaffold, and the quotient-antipode formula. The first finding includes the repeated `hantipode` block as part of its extraction. I did not report the short per-case `by_cases` simp branches or the repeated `universal_detInverse` opening, as they are too small to meet the rubric.

findings.problem: The final `refine` has three blocks that each prove the same step. For an ideal generated by a family, they reduce a vanishing or membership statement for every element to the generators, using `Ideal.span_le.mpr`, `rintro _ ⟨⟨i, j⟩, rfl⟩` and `RingHom.mem_ker`. The setup above them (`q`, `comulQuotient`, the local `CommRing` instance, and the `counit_gen`, `comul_gen` and `antipode_gen` statements) is the same in this file, in UpperTriangularCoordinateRing.ideal_isHopfIdeal_proof, and in UnitriangularCoordinateRing.ideal_isHopfIdeal_proof. In UpperTriangular, lines 151-175 are the same as the target's 156-180 apart from whitespace. In Unitriangular, lines 223-247 are the same. So this generator-to-ideal reduction is written out nine times across three files, with a long GL-specific tail each time.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma in GeneralLinearCoordinateRing, or a small neutral file, with this statement. For `A := GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing K ι`, a family `g : κ → A`, and `I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)`:
- Assume `∀ k, Bialgebra.counitAlgHom K A (g k) = 0`.
- Assume `∀ k, (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K I) (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K I)) (Coalgebra.comul (R := K) (g k)) = 0`.
- Assume `∀ k, HopfAlgebra.antipode K (g k) ∈ I`.
- Conclude `I.IsHopfIdeal K`.

Proof sketch: put the three `Ideal.span_le` blocks in a helper. Prove `I ≤ RingHom.ker f` via `Ideal.span_le.mpr` and `rintro _ ⟨k, rfl⟩` for the counit and comul maps. Prove `I ≤ I.comap antipodeAlgHom` the same way. Then apply `refine { counit_eq_zero := _, map_mkQ_comul_eq_zero := _, antipode_mem := _ }`.

The target then becomes `ideal_isHopfIdeal_of_generators (g := fun p : ι × ι => relation K ι p.1 p.2) counit_gen comul_gen antipode_gen`, keeping only the three `*_gen` facts. UpperTriangular and Unitriangular use the same call with their own `*_gen` facts. In each file the `q`, `comulQuotient` and `CommRing` boilerplate and the three trailing blocks disappear. The local `comul_gen` statement should be restated in the lemma's form, since `comulQuotient` is defined by the same composition. Only the case analysis specific to the subgroup stays in each file.
findings.benefit: Each subgroup file keeps only its own matrix-entry computations, instead of about 25 lines of identical bookkeeping. A change to the `IsHopfIdeal` field shape would be fixed in one place, not three. The proof of `ideal_isHopfIdeal_proof` then shows what differs between the diagonal, upper-triangular and unitriangular cases.

findings.problem: The `antipode_gen` branch proves, inline, that the quotient map sends the antipode of a GL matrix entry to the corresponding entry of the inverse of the pushed-forward universal matrix. It does this by rewriting with `native_antipode_matrix`, then applying `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map`'s `map_inv`, then `congrArg` to extract the entry. The same argument appears in UpperTriangularCoordinateRing (lines 138-149) and again in UnitriangularCoordinateRing's `hinv` and `hantipode` (lines 184-206). Nothing in it is specific to the diagonal, upper-triangular or unitriangular case. It is a fact about any algebra map out of the GL coordinate ring, and GeneralLinearCoordinateRing has no lemma for it. In the target it also sits inside the `¬ i = j` branch of one `by_cases`, so it cannot be reused or tested on its own.
findings.proposed_change: Add to GeneralLinearCoordinateRing a lemma `antipode_matrix_map`. For `B` a commutative `K`-algebra and `q : CoordinateRing K ι →ₐ[K] B`, it states `q (HopfAlgebra.antipode K (matrix K ι i j)) = ((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map q.toRingHom (universal K ι))⁻¹ : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup ι B) i j`. The proof is `rw [native_antipode_matrix]`, then `map_inv` of `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map q.toRingHom`, then `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.coe_inv` or `congrArg` to read off the entry; this is the same sequence as the current inline proof. In the target, the whole `hinv`/`hantipode` pair is replaced by `rw [antipode_matrix_map]`. The `exact ...inv_mem (universal K ι).2 i j hij` then closes the goal, since `universal K ι`'s first component is definitionally the pushed-forward matrix. UpperTriangular does the same, and Unitriangular's local `hantipode` becomes the lemma applied to `q`. The lemma's right-hand side must match `(universal K ι).1⁻¹` up to `rfl`, so a `change` or an `Iff.rfl` bridge may be needed.
findings.benefit: Removes the same non-trivial algebra from three proofs. Each `antipode_gen` then reads as: pass to the inverse of the universal unit, then use closure under inverse in the subgroup. The generic fact is stated once, next to `native_antipode_matrix`, for later quotients such as SL, tori or other subgroups.
